newsitem.title: USA: Analysts Int'l falls after Q4 dips below consensus.
newsitem.headline: Analysts Int'l falls after Q4 dips below consensus.

text.p: Shares of Analysts International Corp, which provides computer software services, fell 3-7/8 to 35-1/8 after the company reported fiscal fourth quarter earnings that were one cent per share below expectations.
"Most of its competitors have met or beat estimates. The fact that they disappointed by a penny has some people concerned," Hanifen Imhoff analyst Lance Marx said.
Earlier, Analysts International reported earnings of $0.29 a share for its fourth quarter ended June 30, up from $0.23 a year ago but below the First Call consensus of $0.30 share.
The company's revenues for the quarter rose to $97.3 million from $72.6 million.

"Demand for information technology services continues to grow very rapidly, which is reflected in the 29 percent growth rate of our core business," Frederick Lang, chairman, said in the earnings statement. "We are proud that much of our growth comes from our existing clients and that we also expand our cleint base every year."
